item.title: Implement retry_budget.py per SPEC.md with focused tests
item.brief: Implement `retry_budget.py` in the repository according to `SPEC.md` at the repository root. Preserve the documented API exactly. Handle every error and boundary case the spec specifies. Add focused tests covering those cases; the existing tests only cover basics. Use the Python standard library only. Commit the work with a clear commit message. Acceptance criteria: every API item and error/boundary case in SPEC.md is implemented and tested; the full test suite passes; no new third-party dependencies. Commit authorship must be the repository's configured git user, with no tool or assistant attribution lines.

pr.body: Approach: retry_delay validates all args first (built-in int only, minimums per SPEC), returns None at the attempt limit, computes min(cap, base*2**(attempt-1)) via _backoff which short-circuits when base>=cap or the doubling count reaches cap.bit_length() (avoids huge powers), applies max with retry_after_ms, and returns None unless elapsed+delay < budget. Key files: retry_budget.py, test_retry_budget.py. Checks: python3 -m unittest -v -> 25 OK; backoff shortcut cross-checked vs naive formula, 0 mismatches. Assumptions: 'built-in int' means type(x) is int, so int subclasses are rejected; invalid types raise ValueError as the spec states. Limits: no upper integer bound, so very large inputs are only bounded by Python int arithmetic on the budget comparison.
pr.summary: Made retry_delay happen. Now can compute bounded retry waits with budget and attempt limits. Before: stub raising NotImplementedError; now: validated, saturating backoff with Retry-After floor and strict budget check, 25 passing tests.
